name: LANKO 701 Duragrout
paste:
LANKO 701 DURAGROUT: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: LANKO 701 Duragrout, May 2025, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/lanko-701-duragrout.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide LANKO 701 Duragrout where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description. LANKO 701 Duragrout is a high strength, dual expanding, Class C structural grout. It is designed to undergo controlled expansion in the plastic state, while counteracting the shrinkage normally associated with portland cement in the hardened state. LANKO 701 Duragrout has been formulated to achieve high early strengths with low water addition levels.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Anchor bolts
    - Underpinning walls
    - Structural column grouting
    - Under heavy machinery
    - Crane rail and conveyor supports
    - Bridge bearings
    - Post tensioned concrete ducts
    - Under precast panels
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.10.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. LANKO 701 Duragrout
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Class C Dual Expanding Structural Grout
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2025, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1478.2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.1).
    - ASTM C348: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Flexural-strength (p.2).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Flowability (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shrinkage compensated in both the plastic and hardened state
    - High strength for precision grouting installations
    - Versatile - can be used in dry pack, plastic and flowable consistencies
    - Extended workable time
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Colour: Grey powder
    - Density: 2,200 kg/m³ - dependent on water addition rate
2.6 Compressive strength.
    | Consistency | 1 Day | 7 Days | 28 Days |
    | Dry Pack | ~ 40 MPa | ~70 MPa | ~ 80 MPa |
    | Plastic | ~ 35 MPa | ~ 50 MPa | ~ 70 MPa |
    | Flowable | ~ 20 MPa | ~ 50 MPa | ~ 60 MPa |
    | Material and curing conditions at 23⁰C / 50% r.h. The results above are tested on 50mm x 50mm cube specimens (Flowable consistency) |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2)
2.7 Flexural-strength.
    | ASTM C348 | Flexural strength |
    | 1 day | ~ 5 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 9.5 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 10.0 MPa |
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: Available in 20 kg (moisture resistant multiwall) bag
    - Shelf life: 6 months
    - Storage conditions: In dry conditions and unopened original packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Surface Preparation.
    - For all surfaces, loose contaminants and unsound concrete must be chipped away so that a reasonably rough, but strong sound surface is provided
    - All surfaces must be free from oil, grease and dust. This particularly applies to the underside of bedplates, bolts, pipes or other materials, which may have surface contact with the grout
    - Holes and depressions may be cleaned with compressed air to remove loose particles
    - The perimeter of any grouting area in a concrete substrate should be sawcut to provide a minimum of 10mm mechanical key for the grout
3.3 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Formwork.
    - The formwork used must be leak proof to allow for free flowing LANKO 701 Duragrout.
    - The formwork should be arranged so that the grout head is maintained on the side above the level of the underside of the base plate. This will allow gravity flow to completely fill the void to be grouted.
    - Formwork should be coated with form oil to allow easy removal of forms.
    - Ensure adequate air holes are provided.
3.4 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Temperature Control. Temperature affects setting time and rate of increase for strength. For optimum performance maintain grout, concrete and/or steel substrates within the range of 18⁰C-25⁰C prior to, during, and for 48 hours after placement of the grout.
3.5 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Primer Preparation.
    - After cleaning, saturate the concrete surface with clean water for approximately 2 hours prior to applying LANKO 701 Duragrout
    - For horizontal hole pours, fill the hole with a twisted rag, which can then be periodically wetted
    - Ensure that no freestanding water is present on surfaces of foundations or in bolt holes. Remove any free water by use of compressed air or dry towels

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Layer thickness: 10mm-100mm thickness
    - Flowability: 400-600mm (flow through) (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Initial set time: ~ 2 hours
    - Final set time: ~ 3 hours
4.3 Mixing ratio.
    | Consistency | Water per 20 kg bag (litre) |
    | Dry Pack | 2.0 L - 2.5 L |
    | Plastic | 2.5 L - 3.0 L |
    | Flowable | 3.0 L - 4.0 L |
4.4 Yield.
    | Dry Pack | Plastic | Flowable |
    | ~ yield/20 kg bag | ~ 10 L | ~ 10.5 L | ~ 11 L |
    | ~ no of bags/1m³ | ~ 98 | ~ 96 | ~ 94 |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.5 Equipment. LANKO 701 Duragrout must be mechanically mixed using a mechanical grout mixer or a suitable drum mixer. The grout mixer will reduce the chances of the mix becoming lumpy or aerated. Smaller quantities should be mixed in clean drum using an electric drill and spiral drill and spiral mixer at a speed of approximately 500 rpm. DO NOT MIX BY HAND.
4.6 Mixing.
    - Mix with an electric drill and paddle or in a pan or revolving barrel type mixer.
    - Do not mix by hand.
    - Allow approximately 5 minutes mixing to achieve maximum results.
    - Place 70% of the required amount of water into the mixing vessel and slowly add the powder while mixing. Gradually add the remainder of the water to achieve the desired consistency.
4.7 Application.
    - LANKO 701 Duragrout grout should be placed within 20 minutes of mixing to gain the benefit of plastic expansion. During that time keep material in mixer well agitated. After this time discard any grout mix that shows signs of stiffening.
    - Flowable LANKO 701 Duragrout may be placed with lowpressure cement grouting equipment or may be hand rodded into restrained sections. High points must be adequately vented to allow entrapped air to escape.
    - Plastic LANKO 701 Duragrout mortar may be rodded into place or trowel handled where freedom of movement permits. Consistency can range from thick cream to smooth plastic.
    - Do not vibrate LANKO 701 Duragrout into position as this may cause segregation of the mix.
    - Dry pack LANKO 701 Duragrout mortar must be firmly pressed or rammed into place. Consistency should allow pressuring into a firm hard ball without cracking.
    - For sealing rebar or steel rods and bolts into bore holes, adhere to the following guidelines. For vertical holes: Position the bar in the hole, and then pour in the flowable LANKO 701 Duragrout. Alternatively, fill the hole with LANKO 701 Duragrout, then insert the rod or bolt into the wet mix, pushing in and pulling back several times to ensure sound bonding.
    - LANKO 701 Duragrout may be pumped for large grouting installations.
    - All applications require curing. Cover the installed grout with wet hessian sheets or spray periodically with water.
    - Placing LANKO 701 Duragrout in unrestrained environments will result in lower final compressive and flexural strength.
    For horizontal holes: Fill the hole with plastic consistency LANKO 701 Duragrout, then insert the rod or bolt, pulling and pushing as above.
4.8 Application - Aggregate Extension.
    - 10mm washed coarse aggregate may be added to LANKO 701 Duragrout for pours over 100mm in depth
    - Add no more than 10kg of aggregate to each 20kg bag of LANKO 701 Duragrout
    - After extending with gravel, do not place LANKO 701 Duragrout in thicker sections than 200mm
4.9 Cleaning of equipment. LANKO 701 Duragrout should be removed from tools and equipment immediately after use with clean water. Any cured material may be removed by mechanical means
4.10 Limitations and important considerations.
    - The strength values mentioned are the average values of laboratory test results.
    - The results on the site may vary due to different environment,curing conditions and test
    - For detailed information on grouting application and guidelines, refer to Sika Grouting Method Statement.
    - Store LANKO 701 Duragrout in dry conditions in unopened original packaging.
    - Never apply to a dry substrate.
    - Do not retemper LANKO 701 Duragrout with additional water
    - Like all cementitious mortars and concrete, LANKO 701 Duragrout must be protected against rapid drying caused by high temperatures and / or strong winds.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature. between 5⁰C and 35⁰C
5.3 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.10):
    - Like all cementitious mortars and concrete, LANKO 701 Duragrout must be protected against rapid drying caused by high temperatures and / or strong winds.
5.4 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Consistency | 1 Day | 7 Days | 28 Days; Dry Pack | ~ 40 MPa | ~70 MPa | ~ 80 MPa; Plastic | ~ 35 MPa | ~ 50 MPa | ~ 70 MPa; Flowable | ~ 20 MPa | ~ 50 MPa | ~ 60 MPa; Material and curing conditions at 23⁰C / 50% r.h. The results above are tested on 50mm x 50mm cube specimens (Flowable consistency) (AS 1478.2)
    - Flowability: 400-600mm (flow through) (AS 1478.2:2005)
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: LANKO 701 Duragrout, May 2025, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/lanko-701-duragrout.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS LANKO 701 Duragrout, version 09/04/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/m/sds-lanko-701-duragrout.pdf
    - Environmental Product Declaration: LANKO 701 Duragrout EPD, version 14/10/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/lanko-701-duragroutepd.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety.
    - Safety Data Sheet is available from https://aus.sika.com
    - Being cement-based, LANKO 701 Duragrout is alkali in nature which can cause dermatitis. When using LANKO 701 Duragrout it is recommended that applicators wear PVC or similar gloves and safety goggles while handling this product.
    - If dust is generated, wear a suitable dust mask.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
